what_it_does: Uni-Render is a reconfigurable hardware accelerator for neural rendering—modern techniques that use neural networks to synthesize 3D images. The problem: different neural rendering methods (NeRF, which uses ray marching; 3DGS, which uses Gaussian splatting; and hybrid approaches) have completely different computational patterns. Existing accelerators are locked into one method, wasting hardware when you switch algorithms. Uni-Render identifies the common primitives all these methods share (ray traversal, Gaussian rasterization, small neural network inference, and blending results) and implements a flexible dataflow engine that dynamically rewires itself to match each algorithm's needs, adapting its processing elements and memory at runtime.
